questions.question: Which two rivers gave Mesopotamia its name as a land between rivers?
choices: Tigris and Euphrates
Nile and Congo
Indus and Ganges
Yellow and Yangtze

questions.question: Which writing system developed in ancient Mesopotamia?
choices: Hieroglyphic writing
Linear B
Cuneiform
The Latin alphabet

questions.question: What material was commonly used for Mesopotamian written records?
choices: Papyrus sheets
Clay tablets
Bamboo strips
Waxed paper

questions.question: What was a ziggurat?
choices: A royal warship
An irrigation wheel
A merchant's caravan
A raised temple structure

questions.question: Which ruler is associated with a famous Babylonian collection of laws?
choices: Hammurabi
Pericles
Augustus
Ashoka

questions.question: Which people developed city-states such as Ur and Uruk?
choices: Phoenicians
Hittites
Sumerians
Minoans

questions.question: What is a city-state?
choices: A province ruled only from a distant capital
A city and surrounding territory governed as a political unit
A temporary camp without a government
A collection of cities sharing no political authority

questions.question: Why was irrigation important in southern Mesopotamia?
choices: It replaced all agricultural labor
It prevented rivers from changing course
It removed the need to store grain
It brought river water to fields in a region with limited rainfall

questions.question: How could agricultural surpluses support urban growth?
choices: They supported people working in crafts, trade, and administration
They required all residents to work only as farmers
They eliminated all demand for storage
They prevented population concentration

questions.question: Why did Mesopotamian cities trade with other regions?
choices: They had no agricultural products to exchange
They were prohibited from producing goods
They sought materials such as timber and metals not abundant locally
They used trade only for military surrender

questions.question: What do early accounting tablets show about writing's uses?
choices: Writing began solely to record modern-style novels
Writing helped record goods, labor, and transactions
Writing was unrelated to administration
Only rulers' personal diaries were written

questions.question: Why did rivers provide both opportunities and risks?
choices: They provided farmland without any seasonal variation
They prevented movement between settlements
They made drought impossible everywhere
They supported farming but could also flood destructively

questions.question: What does Hammurabi's law collection reveal about Babylonian society?
choices: Penalties could vary according to social status
Every resident had identical legal rights
Written law replaced every form of religious belief
The king lacked any role in justice

questions.question: How did polytheism shape Mesopotamian religious life?
choices: People rejected worship and ritual entirely
Every city had only one identical deity
People worshipped multiple gods associated with different powers
Religious practices centered only on ancestor voting

questions.question: How did empires differ from independent city-states?
choices: Empires contained only one farming village
Empires brought multiple peoples and territories under broader rule
City-states could never have armies
Empires had no administrators or taxation

questions.question: Archaeologists find tablets listing grain deliveries. What inference is best supported?
choices: Every resident could read and write
The city had no agricultural activity
Grain was used only for religious decoration
Officials kept organized records of resources

questions.question: A city imports timber and exports textiles. What does this suggest?
choices: Trade connected regions with different resources and products
The city produced everything it needed locally
Imports were unrelated to resource availability
Trade prevented occupational specialization

questions.question: Which comparison of a canal and a ziggurat is accurate?
choices: Both primarily stored military ships
A ziggurat irrigated fields; a canal housed temple ceremonies
A canal managed water; a ziggurat served religious functions
Both were writing systems used by scribes

questions.question: Why should historians avoid treating Mesopotamia as one unchanging kingdom?
choices: The region had no permanent settlements
Different societies and empires ruled the region over time
All its inhabitants spoke one language throughout history
Its political institutions never changed

questions.question: Which evidence best supports a claim about unequal legal treatment?
choices: A map showing two rivers
A tablet listing the month's grain deliveries
A drawing of an irrigation canal
A law assigning different penalties to people of different status
